correctness.rationale: The full positive-eigenvector equations imply a unique root beyond both a and sqrt(Q). A positive eigenvector is reconstructed for the root; its derivative in Q is positive, yielding exact rearrangement extrema. The threshold comparison at 1 treats the case Q>=1 separately. Both rational witness loop gains are exact, and a clean standalone Python checker passed 5,090 supplementary comparisons. The proof applies for all n and positive parameters as specified; finite checks are not extrapolated as proof.

originality.rationale: The new result is the full sharp permutation extremal classification and necessary-and-sufficient invasion criterion for a heterogeneous two-way single-reservoir next-generation matrix with fixed nodewise row sums. The originating work gives row-sum bounds and a two-layer spectral reduction only under layerwise-constant cross-layer sums; our source model violates that condition. Prior correlated-transmission studies establish qualitative correlation effects in different network/stochastic models but do not furnish the displayed cubic factor plus all-permutation sharpness or the two-group row-score-preserving threshold reversal in the materials actually inspected. Classical Perron theory and rearrangement are correctly credited as ingredients, not independently new. A potentially relevant 2025 full text remained inaccessible and is a historical-priority limitation.
residual_risks: The full 2025 stochastic correlation paper could not be inspected because full-text retrieval was restricted; historical priority remains uncertain for broad correlation statements.
A general nonnegative-matrix optimization theorem may imply the specialized proof as a corollary; the proposed scope is only the natural single-reservoir exact classification.
The arbitrary mixing-network analogue and nonlinear endemic dynamics have not been established.

value.rationale: The question is whether node-local epidemic reproduction scores suffice to assess an environmental-contact assignment, a direct issue raised by layered epidemic metric models. For any n and fixed positive shedding/exposure multisets the theorem exactly optimizes invasion via sorting, supplies a necessary-and-sufficient threshold test, and shows the sharp smallest two-group counterexample with all local row sums unchanged but opposite global invasion verdicts. This is a full natural optimization/classification rather than a selected parameter evaluation. Applicability is confined to homogeneous complete human mixing and one reservoir.
